# naming.compiler.introspection-source-and-effect-frontiers

Kind: `native-observation`

## Problem statement

Literal and substituted namespace/info/array calls can select different compiler instructions while source operands mutate visible state. Disassembly alone does not establish the runtime effect order.

## Question

What original operand/cache/disassembly and separate effect-callback rows do the fixed introspection controls observe?

## Conclusion

The immutable 31-body list and compiler tables retain each accepted or rejected case; effect scripts retain their separate native chronology. Dynamic/literal roots, overflow, wrong arity and malformed lists are distinct controls. No result row proves unobserved return state or a source-only ownership grant. Shared selected_worker_operation maps the completed original compiler plan for Generic Array dispatch as well as selected Inline/CompileError paths. A selected Generic Array worker can therefore retain completed original local declarations while still issuing no inline instruction or admission. The authored registration control uses explicit test tokens; it is not a native token/header/process observation. The unchanged C8.6/C9 array17 table supplies its independent observed left/right/a local names and generic instruction. Primitive error propagation also preserves the reached selected String result/header/cache when its projected extent is unchanged; changed extents keep their own source protocol. NativeScalarGetterError::integer_result_producer keeps the reached primitive IntWidthOverflow fresh-result purpose separate from the Invalid append-based String producer and rejects a foreign protocol. The five-release GetInt recipe control does not claim that the same source selects GetInt or the same opcode everywhere: original C9.0 case12 and case13 provide their own distinct observed primary windows. Generic authentic C ArraySet captures the original root before value conversion/parity, preserves original key/value objects through the selected native list-copy or actual dictionary path, and carries the actual selected receiver/member TraceHome across callbacks. The C8.4 value path rereads the same original input; empty-array and parity result presenters retain their independently selected release purposes. Linked API controls assert original software header/operand correspondence and genuine-C-issuer refusal, without issuing a new native object, local table, callback timing or compiler admission observation. Jim and explicit Logical handlers retain their separate purposes.

Array-existence result advice separates C8.4/Jim fresh-integer recipes from the C8.5–9.1 execution-boolean-constant recipe and withholds unknown/hosted provider purposes.

## Scope

Only the original retained programs, capture windows and provider labels in the attached artifacts are covered. Version labels are original receipt metadata, not a fresh patchlevel query. Missing command/API doors and aborted processes stay distinct from successful guest completion. Source files/probes explain the observer protocol; no pinned engine implementation excerpt or executed Rust assertion is claimed. Different attempts and sources are retained separately, never treated as byte-identical duplicates. The linked CmdCore integer error transport control compares the unchanged primitive Int getter String-bad row10 separately for C8.6, C9.0 and C9.1, retaining each release message and error-code classification plus the selected String-result producer. The public primitive fields and software transport identity remain independent from physical Native headers, frames and executed consumer assertions.

Pure recipe selection cannot establish object birth, refcount, primary/residency, live execution-environment identity, frame entry or a completed array lookup. Original native header/local observations keep their exact measured bounds.
